figure_captions.eda_01_rating_distribution.png: Rating 5 is the most common, representing 63.9% of reviews; rating imbalance should be considered when comparing groups.
figure_captions.eda_02_helpfulness_by_rating.png: The lowest observed mean rate is for rating 1 (0.540) and the highest is for rating 5 (0.872); this is descriptive and does not establish causation.
figure_captions.eda_03_review_length_distribution.png: Review length has a median of 302 characters and a 95th percentile of 1203, illustrating the spread between typical and long reviews.
figure_captions.eda_04_helpfulness_by_review_length.png: The longest-review group has a mean helpfulness rate 0.098 higher than the shortest-review group; intermediate groups should be examined for nonlinear patterns.
figure_captions.eda_05_helpfulness_vote_counts.png: The median vote count is 2; 37.7% of valid-rate reviews have only one vote. Rates based on different vote counts have different precision.
figure_captions.eda_06_helpfulness_by_rating_extremity.p: Reviews at extremity 2 have a mean helpfulness rate 0.184 higher than reviews at extremity 0; a formal test is needed to assess the pre-specified directional hypothesis.

interval_note: Plotted intervals are approximate row-level 95% intervals. They are descriptive, not cluster-adjusted confirmatory inference. Formal tests must account for the analysis design.
